requirements.title: Verification Process

evidence.claim: Four human representatives activate a normal verification panel. Governance changes BRN rate, verifier stake and timeout between two votes without resampling the panel or moving its deadline. A third absent voter defaults at the certified deadline; original stake amounts settle, returned stake and the newly verified wallet can spend, all nodes restart and a fresh observer recovers. Controlled clocks and a relay of pinned drand proofs; not partition or adversarial-human evidence.

Signed-history replay selects a committee, certifies a governance timeout change, and activates the same panel under the new duration. The subsequent governed vote and startup authority validation pass. Component evidence, not a live delayed-beacon or partition test.

requirements.note: Active-panel governance transitions have live evidence. This does not sign off every verification outcome, revote, challenge interaction, UI flow or Sybil-resistance claim. Release gates remain closed.

evidence.claim: Live, opt-in breadth-first group trust traversal returns a registered membership path. Cycles, depth and visit bounds, malformed edges, pinned endpoints, changed endorsements and outage classification pass 26 group tests. No node consensus changes.

requirements.title: Handling Bad Actors

evidence.claim: An upheld challenge candidate replays the named cut, applies fraud revocation and bounded bounty backing, and derives the next human roster. Certification requires the previous roster's quorum. Tests reject earlier-cut certificates, altered commitments and incomplete panels.

Seven independent signer stores produce an outcome certificate through replay-checked prevotes and precommits; six of ten human units cannot prepare it. Restart retains the choice, and a selection cannot use a second journal to conflict at the same height. This is a gated signer test, not live network settlement.

Eight independent signer stores exchange typed outcome proposals, votes and decisions through the agreement worker over loopback TCP. Six of ten human units cannot decide; seven do, and a clockless late signer recovers the decision. Restart re-emits the same certificate without installing balances or advancing the selection chain. This is gated agreement, not live outcome settlement.

The gated outcome signer atomically checks ordinary final-vote reservations against its replayed cut and persists a local vote fence with its journal. A stale cut and invalid clock leave no fence; a valid fence blocks ordinary soft and final signatures across restart. This is a local signing boundary, not epoch installation or network-wide finality.

Gated selection/outcome records share a canonical chain. Restart and raw import reconstruct the settled cut and reduced human roster; a revoked human cannot help certify its successor. Replay preserves fraud splits and settlement receipts. Signed tails must name the latest outcome epoch; stale contexts fail closed. This does not install live economics or resume payments.

Seven signed-history tests cover post-outcome clean-remainder spending, inactivity, rejected revoked spending, one-time reward and stake claims, in-flight revocation and rejected return, certificate restart/import, stale contexts, and a challenge panel crossing an epoch before a second outcome. These are replay and record-transfer tests, not live epoch activation.

The sync worker transfers a multi-chunk outcome and its successor selection over loopback TCP, then serves that mixed chain again after reopening the receiver store. Live account snapshots remain unchanged. Signed ledger history is preloaded; this is not full-node bootstrap or live economic settlement.

The gated runtime discovers a completed upheld panel without a supplied candidate, persists its quorum decision, and serves a late observer without a key or clock over TCP. Restart keeps the reduced roster and pauses new epoch signing. Signed history is preloaded; live balances do not change.

Outcome discovery excludes incomplete and rejected panels. A decided signer journal recovers into the canonical chain after reopening the store, without a clock, economic writes, or clearing its ordinary vote fence.

Version-5 wallet blocks sign the installed genesis payment context. Wrong contexts are rejected through real RPC without ledger, election or durable vote changes. Valid payments confirm across restart, and missing or corrupt context metadata stops initialization without repair. This does not install post-outcome state, establish an agreed payment roster or unseal votes.

requirements.note: The gated live journey installs certified fraud settlement and agreed payment authority, rejects old-epoch payments, and recovers after restart and fresh-node catch-up (iteration 78). Roster-only updates also have component and live evidence (iteration 79). Timeout ordering, re-verification and adversarial/Sybil-resistance validation remain open. Production stays gated.

requirements.title: Governance Process

evidence.claim: Three independent human representatives count a delegated ballot, install its activation schedule, refuse an old-epoch post-activation block while three pre-cutoff payments confirm, activate the new rate, and recover through restart and fresh-node catch-up. Uses controlled clocks; does not prove ballot-cut fencing for newly confirmed proposals or partition safety.

After proposal support is cemented, three independent human representatives refuse a post-counting final promise while three pre-counting payments confirm. Ballot and activation certificates install, all three nodes restart, and a fresh fourth observer recovers. Controlled clocks; does not cover final promises made before threshold support cemented or partition safety.

A final support promise and a payment after its counting deadline cannot both be reserved in either order, including after reopening. Soft support does not reserve a deadline. These are component checks, not live partition evidence.

evidence.claim: Three independent human representatives refuse a post-deadline final promise while earlier payments confirm, including after a supported withdrawal. They certify rejection below the endorsement threshold or close the withdrawal without activating changes. New-epoch payments succeed; all three nodes restart and a fresh fourth observer recovers each terminal phase with unchanged rules. Controlled clocks; not a partition test.

Three human representatives certify six checkpoints across overlapping proposals. An existing voting window survives a duration change to zero, a new proposal uses the new window, and RPC deadlines agree. Governed payments, restart of all three nodes and fresh-observer catch-up pass with the original recovery timeout. Controlled clocks and connected local nodes; not partition or production-time evidence.

Signed-history checks preserve existing proposal, voting and counting windows across duration shortening, extension and buffer changes. Lowering the support threshold cannot reopen an expired unsupported proposal. Independent governance accounts depend on their verification history during replay. Component evidence only.

requirements.note: Final promises reserve governance deadlines atomically. Counting, activation, terminal proposal closure and overlapping duration-change proposals have live evidence. W-060 records certified competing constitutional diffs and recovery. Partition recovery and other in-flight rule interactions remain unsigned; release gates stay closed.

requirements.title: Delegation

evidence.claim: An honest 2+1 partition holds scoped revocation below confirmation quorum without changing payment epochs. Healing confirms the revocation on all three nodes; proposal tombstones, replacement parameter grants and the prior certified count survive activation, payment, all-node restart and fresh-observer catch-up. The fixture explicitly supplies the owner's direct vote instead of relying on blanket fallback through a scoped grant. Controlled clocks, not Byzantine or partitioned secondary-ballot evidence.

Honest 2+1 partitions prevent a secondary ballot from confirming and prevent the delegated counting epoch from installing without quorum. Healing completes both. Four transitive/direct-owner proposal tallies, scope revocations, discovery, activation and a governed payment survive all-node restart and fresh-observer recovery. Controlled clocks; not Byzantine or production-scale evidence.

Iteration 116: three independent human nodes accepted owner-signed encrypted proposal and parameter grants, rejected secondary-key account signatures and foreign-chain grants, and preserved revocation tombstones and replacement generations through certified counting/activation, all-node restart and fresh-observer catch-up. Canonical journal snapshots agreed. Controlled clocks. Journal-only evidence; iteration 117 replaces whole-registry storage with per-scope records and separately tests secondary ballots.

Three independent human nodes admit historical-grant secondary ballots, reject forged signatures, wrong recipients, wrong grant dependencies and duplicate choices, and count a transitive A-to-B-to-C chain with direct-owner precedence. Proposal revocation before or after a candidate removes delegated weight at the certified cut; revocation after counting does not rewrite the result. The passing change activates and a governed payment confirms. Restart and a fresh observer preserve all four proposal results and byte-identical per-scope records. Controlled clocks, not partition or native desktop evidence.
Cut projection drops votes across unverified intermediates or recipients, replaced grant generations, cycles and excessive depth. Proposal grants and revocation tombstones override parameter scope.

Discovery reads owner and recipient indexes from one storage snapshot. The live journey finds and decrypts a grant, removes revoked recipient authority, reads exact outgoing scope generations, and repeats these checks after all-node restart and fresh-node catch-up. A restart bug using governed parameters for the genesis identity was corrected to use the persisted original parameters.

Real Tauri/WebKit controls register parameter and proposal grants, discover encrypted grants, submit two secondary ballots, and revoke one grant before counting. Stale generations, changed genesis, wrong wallet, revoked grants and locked signers are rejected. Three independent human nodes certify two supporting votes rather than three, activate the proposal, restart, and recover the same result and indexes on a fresh observer. Public fixture keys, controlled setup/counting clocks and wall-time desktop signing; not partition or production packaging evidence.

requirements.note: Secondary ballots, transitive counting and paginated grant discovery have gated native certified recovery evidence. Iteration 119 adds real desktop registration, secondary ballots and revocation with certified counting, restart and fresh-observer recovery. Iterations 154 and 156 add honest partitions at scoped revocation, secondary-ballot admission and counting, followed by activation and recovery.
